test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 11 Oct 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The internal and external radii of a hollow hemispherical bowl are 20 cm and 23 cm, respectively. What is the total surface area (in cm²) of the bowl?
solution:
**Given**

Internal Radius = 20 cm

External Radius = 23 cm

**Formula used**

Total surface area = 3πR² + πr²

where R and r are the external and internal radii of the hemisphere respectively.

**Calculation**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b01a13eaf7cb0c11108a2469a18de65dc2b2f9a2e157519ac1bd83679ab98474.png] 

Total surface area = 3π(23)² + π(20)²

⇒ π( 3 × 23 × 23 + 20 × 20)

⇒ π(1587 + 400)

⇒ 1987π cm²

**∴ The total surface area (in cm2) of the bowl is 1987π cm². 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

 
• The curved surface area of the outer hemisphere = 2πr2
 
• The curved surface area of the inner hemisphere = 2πr2
 
• If we observe the figure given above, we can see that a ring is formed. The Area of the ring = π(R2 - r2)
 
• So, the Total surface area of the hollow hemisphere can be calculated if we add the formulas given above, that is, TSA of a hollow hemisphere = 2πR2 + 2πr2+ π(R2 - r2). This can be written as TSA of hollow hemisphere = 2π(R2 + r2) + π(R2 - r2). And if we want to simplify it further, it becomes 3πR2 + πr2so, The Total surface area of the hollow hemisphere is 3πR2 + πr2
